author: Jackson Thomas
title: Tragedy Strikes Kentucky Family as Car Crash Claims Two Lives Near Louisville
text:
A Kentucky woman has been left with unspeakable grief after her husband and their one-year-old daughter died in a car crash while on the way home from their honeymoon.
The father, 22, and Oakleigh (pictured together) were pronounced dead at the scene after both vehicles went up in flames The tragedy unfolded on Saturday afternoon in Hardinsburg, about an hour outside of Louisville, when a Ford F-150 crossed the center lane and struck the family’s Chevrolet Silverado.
According to the Kentucky State Police, the collision caused both vehicles to go up in flames, resulting in the immediate deaths of Hunter Lyons, 22, and their daughter, Oakleigh Lyons.
Macey Lyons, Hunter’s new wife and Oakleigh’s mother, was flown to University of Louisville Hospital with non-life-threatening burn injuries.
The other driver, Joseph Maynard, 48, also died at the scene.
The circumstances surrounding Maynard’s decision to cross into the opposite lane remain unclear, with authorities stating the cause of the crash is still under investigation.
article image The newlywed couple, Hunter and Macey, had just celebrated their wedding on July 19, as revealed in a Facebook post by Hunter’s family.
Their daughter, Oakleigh, was born in February 2024, bringing immense joy to the family before the heartbreaking accident.
At the time of the crash, the couple was returning from their honeymoon in Pigeon Forge, a journey that had been filled with hope and new beginnings.
Hunter’s mother, Leigh Ann Payne-Weisser, shared the devastating news on social media, revealing that the family was on their way home when their lives were irrevocably changed.
The loss has left the community in shock, with many struggling to process the tragedy.
The family’s car was struck by a Ford F-150, driven by Joseph Maynard, 48, after he crossed into the center lane ‘for unknown reasons’ In the wake of the accident, the local community has rallied around Macey Lyons, offering support as she grapples with the sudden loss of her husband and daughter.
A close friend set up a Venmo account to accept donations for her recovery, while several local businesses have joined efforts to raise funds.
Doe Valley Golf Club contributed over $1,500, and Calhoun Baptist Church is organizing a fundraiser to help cover funeral costs and medical expenses.
An online silent auction will also be held in honor of Hunter and Oakleigh, with proceeds going to the family.
These gestures of solidarity have provided some comfort to Macey during this unimaginably difficult time.
Hunter and Macey got married on July 19 and were on their way back from their honeymoon when their lives changed forever The emotional toll on the family has been profound.
Hunter’s mother, Payne-Weisser, shared a poignant message on Facebook, reflecting on the loss of her son and granddaughter.
She wrote that on the anniversary of the death of her other son, Garrett, who passed away two years ago, she believes he has been watching over Hunter and Oakleigh. ‘It is my belief that Garrett has been watching over us and was there with open arms to welcome them home,’ she wrote, accompanied by photos of her late son and grandson.
Other loved ones have also expressed their sorrow, with one friend describing the tragedy as ‘shaking the world to the core’ and urging prayers for Macey’s strength.
As the investigation into the crash continues, the community remains united in mourning and supporting Macey Lyons.
The accident serves as a stark reminder of the fragility of life and the profound impact such tragedies can have on families and entire communities.
For now, the focus remains on helping Macey navigate the grief and beginning the process of healing, even as questions about the crash linger unanswered.
